title: Interrelation of uric acid and ethanol metabolism in man
authors: Lieber CS, Jones DP, Losowsky MS, Davidson CS
population: 22 adults aged 31 to 67 years without gout, including 16 acutely intoxicated patients and 7 subjects given ethanol on a metabolic ward
funder: Work supported in part by the U. S. Army Medical Research and Development Command, Department of the Army, contract DA-49-193-MD-2013, and by a grant from the Nutrition Foundation, Inc., N. Y.
result: In eight acutely intoxicated patients (mean serum ethanol 311 mg per 100 ml), blood lactate averaged 22.3 mg per 100 ml, against a mean of 7.1 mg per 100 ml in 18 fasting normal subjects. Oral or intravenous ethanol raised serum uric acid in seven subjects; in three, urinary uric acid output fell to about 20 to 50% of control values without change in creatinine clearance, and oral sodium lactate reproduced the fall in one subject.
